text.text: Every pound that enters the building is weighed, dated and recorded. That one habit keeps shelves honest and donors thanked.
At the door
Weigh the delivery and open the Donations table. Find the expected row or add a new one.
Check dates, dented cans and cold-chain items. Set aside anything unsafe and write why in the notes.
Link the donation to the stock line it belongs on, or add a new stock line.
Press Mark received. Then update Pounds on hand on the stock line.
Afterwards
Thank the donor the same week.
Rotate older stock to the front of the shelf.
Keep a tally of anything turned away so you can explain why.
Distribution day is where everything the team has done meets the neighbors it was done for. The goal is a calm line and a dignified experience.
Before doors open
Open the distribution row and press Open doors
Check the cooler temperature and write it down
Set up tables from fresh to dry, so cold items go last
Brief greeters: friendly, no questions about why someone is here
While open
Check each household in using its number, not its name, where possible.
Offer choice where you can: a table with options beats a pre-packed box.
Keep a clear path for people using wheelchairs and strollers.
After closing
Enter households served and pounds given out
Update stock on hand for the big items
Note what ran out first
Thank every volunteer by name
Safe food is not optional. Follow your local health rules; this page is a working reminder, not a replacement for them.
Keep it cold, keep it clean
Check cooler and freezer temperatures at open and close and write them down.
Wash hands before handling food and after handling boxes.
Never give out food past a date your local rules say must be discarded.
When in doubt

cells.text: Set aside and discard; note it on the donation
Do not refreeze; follow local guidance or discard
Ask the donor; if unknown, do not distribute
Show the label; do not guess
